sources.title: A Year of Fast Apply — The Path to 10k Tokens per Second
sources.evidence: Reopened the complete original article from a fresh HTTP 200 fetch on October 27, 2026. The October 29, 2025 retrospective identifies Apply 3 and its 256k native context. Its only size disclosure is a 3–8B range for the open-source coding backbones used across the Apply series; it does not name Apply 3’s base model or give an individual nominal total. It says the base remains intact during LoRA SFT, but that cannot establish a count without an identified base. Apply 3 uses approximately 145k examples, rank 128, alpha 32, BF16 training and FP8 deployment. No separately defined active count appears; adapter trainability, quantization and speculative decoding do not supply one.

sources.title: Apply Code API reference and complete request/response schema
sources.evidence: Names relace-apply-3 as the replacement for earlier Apply versions. Table specifies 128k maximum input and 128k maximum output. API consumes initial_code, edit_snippet and optional instruction, and returns mergedCode. OpenAI-compatible calls still require code/update tags. The full Apply schema contains no caller-defined tools, tool results or reasoning channel. MIT in OpenAPI info licenses the API specification, not model weights.

sources.title: Agent Tool Definition
sources.evidence: Shows an external coding agent calling edit_file, whose implementation sends existing code and edits to the Apply API, receives mergedCode, writes the file and returns a diff. Apply is the implementation behind a tool; the example does not show Apply choosing or invoking tools itself.

sources.title: Relace Terms of Use
sources.evidence: Describes the core service as API access to company code-generation models; inference occurs in company systems. Grants limited, nontransferable, revocable service access, reserves intellectual-property rights and prohibits unauthorized distribution and reverse engineering. Supports proprietary hosted-service classification, not an open model-weight license.

sources.title: Open models quickstart
sources.evidence: Separates purpose-built Relace code models from third-party open-weight models that Relace also hosts. Current table lists DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi variants, not Apply 3. Their extended-thinking/tool-calling instructions and weight licenses cannot be transferred to Apply 3.

sources.title: Relace blog archive
sources.evidence: Inspected archive and the linked May 25 2025 Instant Apply article, October 8 2025 Series A article, October 29 Apply 3 retrospective and later Search/Compact technical articles. The earlier two articles do not name Apply 3. No original Apply 3 release-day announcement was recovered.

sources.title: Exploiting parallel tool calls to make agentic search 4x faster
sources.evidence: Fresh full original December 8, 2025 article rechecked October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). It distinguishes earlier SFT-trained Fast Apply from the new RL-trained search agent. The comparisons concern search accuracy and latency; neither an exact Apply 3 parameter-count row nor a named Apply 3 backbone is supplied. Search-model training and tool-use disclosures do not establish Apply 3 total or active counts.

sources.title: Relace Compact: 50k TPS for 50% cost savings
sources.evidence: Fresh full original July 13, 2026 article rechecked October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200). It mentions Fast Apply as reducing edit-output costs, but the compaction/caching analyses and figures supply no Apply 3 total or active count and no named unchanged-base relationship. Compact is separately described as a modified LLM for token-level classification; its identity and methods cannot be transferred to Apply 3.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Apply 3 endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Returns Relace as endpoint provider, 256000 total context, 128000 maximum completion, text input/output and FP8. created=1758891572 is September 26 2025 12:59:32 UTC, establishing a provider record timestamp rather than earliest developer release. supported_parameters contains stop, seed, max_tokens; generic supports_tool_choice flags are nevertheless all true, a metadata inconsistency that cannot override Relace’s task-specific contract.

sources.title: Relace public GitHub repository inventory
sources.evidence: Rechecked the public relace-ai GitHub organization directly on October 27, 2026 at 17:43 UTC (HTTP 200): vite-template and claude-plugins, with no Apply 3 checkpoint, configuration or model card. The fresh Hugging Face search is recorded separately. These negative discovery checks supplement, rather than establish alone, the documented proprietary API distribution.

sources.title: Current complete Relace documentation — parameter re-audit
sources.evidence: Fresh complete documentation fetched October 27, 2026 at 17:41 UTC (HTTP 200), independently searched for Apply 3, parameter counts and named-base lineage. Apply’s model table gives speed and input/output limits only. The open-model list hosts separate third-party models and supplies no Apply 3 lineage. No total or activated-parameter specification was recovered. Exact-model searches for parameters, active/activated counts, base model and original research comparisons likewise found no original count disclosure.

sources.title: Fresh Hugging Face model discovery for Relace
sources.evidence: Fresh HTTP 200 request on October 27, 2026 at 17:43 UTC returned an empty array. No public Relace Apply 3 card/config or named-base lineage was recovered through this search; a negative inventory is supplemental evidence, not proof that no public release exists.

name.note: Official model name; relace-apply-3 is the documented API identifier.

developer.note: Relace develops the specialized model; Squack Inc. is the service’s legal company name.

family.note: Lowercase identifier for the explicitly documented Apply model series.

release_date.note: September 26 2025 is the OpenRouter record creation/listing date. October 29 is a retrospective, not an explicit first release. Neither establishes the earliest developer launch, and even its month remains unverified; clear the baseline date.

open_weights.note: Distributed through proprietary model API access. The public service terms reserve its rights; hosted third-party open models and open training-method descriptions are separate. No public Apply 3 weight release was located.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the model service. Do not mistake the OpenAPI document’s MIT metadata for a model-weight license, or inherit an unidentified backbone’s license.

parameters_b.note: No individual nominal total or named base is disclosed for Apply 3. The developer’s 3–8B range covers Apply-series backbones and cannot select one scalar. LoRA preserves its unnamed base, so the published relationship does not resolve nominal size.

active_parameters_b.note: No separately stated active count or original research-team active-parameter comparison for exact Apply 3 was recovered. LoRA trainable weights are not active inference parameters; neither the series size range nor speculative decoding establishes this count.

architecture.note: LoRA SFT, FP8 and the Transformers library are disclosed methods, not an exact architecture. No named backbone or dense/MoE claim was recovered.

context_window.note: Advertised 256k total capacity; provider gives the decimal integer. Direct Apply API separately caps input and output at 128k each. The 64k SFT training length is not the serving limit.

modalities.note: Initial code, edit snippet and instruction are strings; response is merged-code text. No image, audio or video contract is exposed.

reasoning.note: The Apply endpoint exposes direct merged code without a reasoning channel/control, but no explicit model-level non-reasoning declaration was recovered. Clear the baseline false instead of borrowing the capabilities of separately hosted open models.

tool_call.note: For the documented Apply service, request/response schemas implement a code merge, with no model-selected function calls or tool-result loop. The edit_file integration is another agent calling Apply as a tool, not Apply calling tools.

description.value: Specialized code-editing model that merges an edit snippet into an existing source file and returns the updated code.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported general-purpose chat, writing and analysis description with the documented code-merge task.

patch.description: Specialized code-editing model that merges an edit snippet into an existing source file and returns the updated code.
patch.notes: Relace Apply 3 merges code edits; OpenAI-compatible transport does not make it a general-purpose chat model. The documented total context is 256k, with 128k input and 128k output API limits. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed: Relace gives only a 3–8B range for Apply-series backbones, without naming Apply 3’s base. Architecture is also undisclosed. September 26 2025 is an OpenRouter listing timestamp, while October 29 is a training retrospective; earliest release remains unverified. Apply can be invoked by an agent’s edit tool, but its own API returns merged code rather than tool calls. A model-level reasoning declaration was not found.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained null total and active counts after rereading the original training article, current complete docs, later Search/Compact research and public model inventories, plus fresh exact-model/lineage/active-count searches. The published 3–8B backbone range is series-wide; the unnamed LoRA base cannot support an individual nominal count, and no active-count convention was found. Explicit null patch values and parameters_source are recorded. The other 12 assessments are unchanged, including the specialized merge description, proprietary classification, unverified earliest release/reasoning declaration and documented 256k context.
